text:
sam: noticed NA2 serving latency spike ~10:10 UTC, p95 went from 120ms -> 900ms, error rate climbing. Appears to correlate with kv-cache client timeouts in the runtime logs.

olivia: looking at metrics now, cache hit rate dropped ~35% at 10:09 and batching queues grew. RL scheduler showing backlog on pool-gpu-na2-hot.

marta: any deploys around then? deploy-bot: deploy triggered by ci at 10:07 UTC: runtime v2.7.3 -> v2.8.0 (kvcache batch refactor).

kevin: that refactor had a change to the async eviction logic, I flagged a potential race but it passed tests.

olivia: logs show repeated `kvcache:Get() timeout 200ms` and then evictions flood. Example stack: ```runtime/kvcache/evict.go:45 kvcache:evict triggered -> mgr:EvictAll -> net:close connection```

sam: traffic currently hitting NA2 region only. Can we route heavy customers to NA1 temporarily?

marta: oncall-bot: runbook suggests failover via routing service. I can initiate traffic-shift for non-enterprise routes only. Need thumbs. :thumbsup:

kevin: do it. Also roll back the kvcache refactor on NA2 nodes and restart runtime daemons. Rollback safer than hotpatch here.

olivia: scaling note — autoscaler didn't spin new GPUs because hotpool capacity is at hard cap (reserved capacity). We can spin on-demand g2 nodes but cost spike. Thoughts?

sam: prioritize latency over cost for 1h. Use on-demand to buy breathing room, then revert and do controlled rollout.

marta: starting routing shift now for routes tagged `@non-enterprise` -> region:NA1, gradual 20% steps. I'll monitor error rates.

(10:25) deploy-bot: traffic-shift step 1 applied: 20% -> NA1

olivia: p95 down from 900ms -> 320ms after step 2 (40%). Errors trending down.

kevin: starting rollback of runtime on NA2: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/runtime -n infra --to-revision=2` on hotpool nodes, then restart sidecars. I will sequence across AZs.

sam: please also disable batching tuning that was enabled in 2.8 for NA2 (`BATCH_MAX_DELAY_MS=8` -> revert to 4). That was part of the refactor.

kevin: applied env change and scaled restart to 30% of pods to avoid thundering herd.

(10:48) marta: traffic shift at 80% -> NA1, NA2 still handling 20% of legacy and enterprise. Latencies look stable for shifted traffic.

(11:02) deploy-bot: rollback completed on NA2 to v2.7.3 where kv-cache behavior is stable.

olivia: after rollback p95 on NA2 back to ~140ms. KV hit rate recovering.

sam: good. costs — we used 6 on-demand gpus for 45m. Finance: estimate ~+$4.2k extra for emergency capacity this window. We'll tag cost to incident budget.

kevin: follow-ups: add an integration test that simulates KV eviction storms, add circuit-breaker in kvcache client for short-lived timeouts, and introduce a staging rollout policy to gate async eviction changes.

marta: I'll file a postmortem and include rollback timeline, traffic-shift runbook notes, and cost summary.

sam: nice work, team. Add a short alert: when kv-cache hit-rate drops >20% and batching queue >X for 2m, fire pager. Current alert was only p95 latency.

olivia: creating PR for the alert and the runbook tweaks.

kevin: also let's add a temporary protection to routing service to allow instant global failover for enterprise routes in case of cross-region failures.

marta: agreed. I'll include that in the PM for infra resiliency.

sam: closing loop — set incident severity to sev2 and tag oncall notes. I'll ping customers via status page for users impacted by NA2.

oncall-bot: incident annotated: sev2, incident-1847604321, responders: sam, olivia, kevin, marta.

sam: thanks everyone. once the postmortem is up drop it here. :white_check_mark:
